clauses.reason: The only operative sentence of EO 8031 revokes Executive Order No. 4130 of January 22, 1925, which withdrew public land in Oregon for use as a fish hatchery. The order states no later effective date and no condition, so the revocation operated by the order's own words when the order was made; the order is dated January 9, 1939. The command was therefore exhausted by performance on 1939-01-09. The filing line of the held Federal Register page gives January 10, 1939 as the filing date and the issue is dated January 12, 1939 (4 FR 193); a reading that dates the operation of the revocation to filing or publication is the alternative, but the order itself names neither as its effective date. The surviving consequence is the end of the withdrawal of that land, a completed change and not a continuing command of this order.

research_rationale:
EO 8031 (January 9, 1939) revokes Executive Order No. 4130 of January 22, 1925, withdrawing public land in Oregon for a fish hatchery, under the act of June 25, 1910 (36 Stat. 847). I read the held text of the Federal Register page (4 FR 193), which contains the whole order, its signature line, its date and its filing line, and compared the clause inventory with it: the order has one operative sentence. A self-executing revocation is exhausted when it takes effect; here that is the date of the order, and the filing and publication dates are disclosed as alternative readings. No later instrument affecting this order was found in the held corpus. The held text is the machine-extracted text layer of the Federal Register issue; OCR wording remains subject to a page check against the PDF, which is not held.

savings.reason: The order has no savings or transition clause. The revocation changed the legal status of the withdrawn land by ending the withdrawal of Executive Order No. 4130; that completed change, not any continuing command of this order, is the surviving consequence, and it is recorded as accrued. No held source shows any other residual effect.
